text:
Shayne Gostisbehere won the Stanley Cup with Carolina last spring, and at 33 he's still the defenseman the Hurricanes hand the puck to when they want offense. He has 16 points in 22 games, half of them on the power play.

The five-on-five numbers are startling: Carolina takes 66% of shot attempts and 64.6% of expected goals with him on the ice. That's a team built to tilt the rink, and Evolving-Hockey's adjustments last season said he does drive play himself, 86th percentile among defensemen once teammates and opponents are accounted for.

Here's the caution. Carolina has scored nearly eight more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and that kind of on-ice luck fades. His own shooting is unremarkable, three goals on 2.9 expected, so the points depend on teammates finishing.

The most recent headline wasn't about offense. In Thursday's overtime loss to Montreal he drilled Lane Hutson, who was left dazed, as Cory Lavalette of North State Journal reported.

What to watch: if the bounces cool, does his point pace hold through the power play alone?
headline: Gostisbehere's numbers come with a tailwind
